Contactless electroreflectance (CER) spectroscopy was used to study GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures with Mn concentrations ranging from 0.1% to 7%.
The Fermi level in (Ga,Mn)N with x > 0.1% was found to be located approximately 1.25 - 1.55 eV above the valence band edge.
The Fermi level position was independent of the GaN cap thickness, indicating it is predominantly determined by the bulk properties of (Ga,Mn)N.
For low-x (Ga,Mn)N (x < 0.1%), the Fermi level was found to be closer to the conduction band edge, similar to the position at the GaN surface.
The data allowed an estimation that the (Ga,Mn)N band gap change compared to GaN predominantly takes place in the valence band, decreasing by 0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % of Mn.
The strong mid-gap Fermi level pinning and good insulating properties of (Ga,Mn)N make it a promising material for use as a highly resistive buffer layer in GaN-based devices.
The CER measurements confirmed the presence of built-in electric fields in the GaN cap layers, with field strengths ranging from 18 kV/cm for low-x samples to over 100 kV/cm for high-x samples.
The Fermi level position in (Ga,Mn)N was found to be close to the Mn-related impurity band, located approximately 1.4 - 1.8 eV above the valence band edge.
The negligible surface depletion layer in high-x (Ga,Mn)N samples indicates the Fermi level is strongly pinned in the middle of the band gap, both in the bulk and at the surface.
The high resistivity and strong insulating properties of (Ga,Mn)N make it a promising alternative to Fe or C doped GaN as a buffer layer in GaN-based transistors and other high power devices.
